newsitem.title: FRANCE: No EU grain export move this week - officials.
newsitem.headline: No EU grain export move this week - officials.

text.p: The European Union has no plans to open up export tenders for the coming harvest at this week's Brussels grain talks, European grain officials said on Thursday.

The issue was not discussed at a member country experts' meeting on Thursday morning and -- barring a last-minute reversal -- will not be on the agenda for formal cereals management committee talks later on Thursday afternoon.
"There will be nothing today," one official said, while others predicted there would be no fresh move on exports until after the next EU farm ministers' meeting on Monday and Tuesday.

The Commission has promised to unblock stalled grain exports in coming weeks but says it is in no hurry actually to start selling forward from this year's crop despite criticism from French farmers who accuse it of losing markets.
One official said the most likely date for first discussions on exports for 1997/98 (July/June) was June 26 -- after ministerial farm talks.
The Commission is seen unwilling to take any decisions on exports which could narrow its room for manoeuvre when proposing the set-aside rate for 1998. The current rate is five percent.
Set-aside is a key part of the annual package which EU's 15 farm ministers are due to start debating next week.
The main grain item on Thursday's formal agenda is the tender for preferential maize imports to Spain. The tender, in which importers can bid for tariff cuts, was reduced to 550,000 tonnes last week.
A total 334,203 tonnes of imported maize has been awarded under the scheme, mainly from the United States but unusually including around 120,000 tonnes from Argentina.
A remaining 215,797 tonnes of maize is open at Thursday's meeting, which is the penultimate chance to bid for tariff reductions before the tender expires on June 26.
A preparatory meeting of EU cereals experts in Brussels on Thursday morning forcused mainly on rice.
